charts.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Equity (incl. NCI)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

equityNci.title: Equity including non-controlling interests
equityNci.content:
Shareholders' equity belongs to Woori Financial Group's own shareholders; total equity including NCI adds the minority stakes consolidated subsidiaries carry on top of that.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the gap between the two lines is the NCI slice -- capital the group controls and reports on its balance sheet but does not own outright, so it should be stripped out of any per-share book-value or ROE comparison.

What to watch:

  • NCI share of total equity widening after an acquisition or subsidiary IPO
  • Using total equity (incl. NCI) instead of parent equity would overstate ROE attributable to common shareholders

nii.title: Net interest income
nii.content:
Net interest income (NII) is interest earned on loans and securities less interest paid on deposits and borrowings -- the core spread-based revenue of a bank holding company.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: NII is the single largest driver of Woori's top line, dwarfing fee and trading income; its trend tracks loan growth and the net interest margin set by Bank of Korea policy rates.

What to watch:

  • NII growth driven by volume (loan book growth) versus margin (rate spread)
  • NII compression when policy rates fall faster than funding costs reprice

deposits.title: Customer deposits
deposits.content:
Customer deposits are the funds retail and corporate customers hold with Woori Bank -- the primary, lowest-cost funding base for the loan book.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: deposit growth funds loan growth without resorting to more expensive wholesale borrowing, so it is a leading indicator for both NII and balance-sheet expansion.

What to watch:

  • Deposits growing slower than loans (forces wholesale funding, pressures margin)
  • Shift from low-cost demand deposits to higher-cost time deposits

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Woori Financial Group Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
